facts.claim: Other name 'Surat wa-l-Duha' (Bukhari, many tafsirs; quran.com); no Companion report fixing the name

Main message: consolation during a pause in revelation - not forsaken, not displeased; the future better; past favours recalled; gratitude through kindness to the orphan and the asker and speaking of Allah's blessing
Sahih: the Prophet was ill and did not stand for night prayer for one-two / two-three nights; an (unnamed) woman taunted that his 'devil' had left him; 93:1-3 revealed
Sahih: Jibril was slow to come; the mushrikun said 'Muhammad has been forsaken' (Muslim 1797a); a Quraysh woman said it (Bukhari 1125)
Sahih: a woman said 'O Messenger of Allah, I think your companion has delayed coming to you'; 93:3 revealed (Bukhari 4951)

Who said it: unnamed in the sahih matn; Umm Jamil (Abu Lahab's wife) in other reports (Ibn 'Ashur via Ibn 'Atiyya/Ibn 'Abbas, Qurtubi via Tha'labi, Ma'ariful, Tafheem, quran.com); Khadija for the gentle wording - mursal, 'not preserved' (Ibn Kathir). Video: no name

Length of the pause: sahih one-two / two-three nights; Ibn 'Abbas 'days'; 12 (Ibn Jurayj), 15 (Ibn 'Abbas), 25 (qila), 40 (Muqatil) days per Qurtubi, who calls Bukhari's the most sahih; Tafheem '12 to 40 days'. Video: 'kuch raatein'

This short pause is distinct from the long 'fatrat al-wahy' after the first revelation (Ma'ariful: two pauses; Tafheem: early breaks frequent; Qurtubi/Ibn Kathir tie al-Duha to Jundub's short pause; Ibn 'Ashur does not link it to the fatra). Video must not call it 'the fatrat al-wahy'

Puppy (jirw) died under the bed, Khawla swept it out, surah revealed (Tabarani al-Kabir 21102; listed among views by Qurtubi) - chain through little-known narrators, no grade shown, contradicts the sahih cause; Ibn Hajar's rejection reported but not opened
The Prophet told Mu'adh (long Isha recitation) to recite surahs like al-Shams, al-Duha, al-Layl, al-A'la (Sahih Muslim 465, Sufyan's narration via Abu al-Zubayr - Jabir)
facts.grade: maana hua (sahih) - single collection, video optional

facts.claim: Takbir after al-Duha to the end of the Quran (al-Bazzi report; Abu Hatim/al-'Uqayli weaken the narrator; 'takbir in joy' reason has no chain per Ibn Kathir; Hakim calls the chain sahih per Qurtubi; Ma'ariful: qurra sunnah)
facts.grade: chhoda gaya (grade ikhtilaaf; not for the video)

facts.claim: 93:1 - by the forenoon light
93:2 - and the night when it settles and covers (all)
93:3 - your Lord has neither left you nor become displeased
93:4 - what comes later (the Hereafter) is better for you than the first (this world)
93:5 - your Lord will give you and you will be pleased
93:6 - did He not find you an orphan and give you refuge
93:7 - and found you unaware of the way and guided you
93:8 - and found you in need and made you self-sufficient
93:9 - so do not oppress the orphan
93:10 - and do not repel the one who asks
93:11 - and speak of the blessing of your Lord
duha = forenoon when sunlight spreads; oath by that light, a sign of Allah's power
saja = the night settles/becomes still and its darkness covers (Qatada, Mujahid, Ibn Zayd, 'Ikrima, Dahhak)
Link of the oath to the pause: night after day is not displeasure; revelation like daylight, the pause like the night's rest
wadda'a = bid farewell/leave; qala = hate/be displeased; object pronoun dropped for verse-end rhythm; verse 3 answers the oath; 'has not hated you since He loved you'
93:4 two compatible meanings: Hereafter better than this world (Ibn Kathir, Ma'ariful a, Qurtubi/Ibn Ishaq); every later stage better than the earlier (Ma'ariful b, Tafheem)

93:5 what will be given: success of the deen in this world (Qurtubi/Ibn Ishaq, Tafheem) and in the Hereafter intercession/Kawthar/being pleased regarding his ummah (Ibn Kathir, Qurtubi); Sahih Muslim 202 'sanurdika fi ummatika'
Orphanhood: father died before birth, mother when he was 6, grandfather 'Abd al-Muttalib when he was 8, then uncle Abu Talib raised and protected him
93:7 'dall' here = unaware (of the Book and details of the shariah before prophethood, cf. 42:52), NOT astray in belief/sin; he was free of idolatry and sin

93:8 'a'il = in need (with dependents); enriched - trade partnership with Khadijah then marriage (Ma'ariful, Tafheem); poor-patient and rich-thankful (Ibn Kathir); true richness is contentment of the soul (Bukhari 6446)
93:9 do not oppress/humiliate the orphan or take his right; Qatada 'be like a merciful father to the orphan'; Bukhari 5304 orphan-carer with the Prophet in Paradise like two fingers
93:10 sa'il = (a) beggar - give a little or refuse gently (Qatada), (b) one who asks for knowledge/guidance - answer gently (Sufyan; Abu al-Darda', Hasan Basri, Sufyan Thawri per Tafheem)
93:11 speaking of Allah's blessing = gratitude (not pride); ni'mah = Quran/prophethood (Mujahid) and all blessings; Abu Dawud 4811 / Tirmidhi 1954 'whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah'
Three favours (6-8) mirrored by three commands (9-11): orphan -> orphan, unaware/guided -> the one who asks, in need/enriched -> speak of the blessing
